name: UCC25600DR
title: UCC25600: 8-pin resonant mode (LLC half-bridge) controller
summary: A variable-frequency controller for LLC resonant half-bridge DC-DC converters of about 100 W to 1 kW, in an 8-pin SOIC. Its oscillator runs from 40 kHz to 350 kHz, with the minimum frequency held to 4% (3% from -20 °C to 105 °C); the maximum frequency is programmable, dead time is set by one resistor and soft-start time by one capacitor. Two gate outputs (0.4 A source, 0.8 A sink) drive a gate drive transformer, and it guards against overcurrent with a restart level and a latch level, bias undervoltage and overvoltage, and overtemperature, with burst mode at light load.

1 V restart level, 2.0 V latch level (typ)

notes: Material type is Production for all seven. The UCC25600D parts ship in tubes of 75 and are MSL level 2; the UCC25600DR parts ship on reels of 2500 and are MSL level 1.

pins.name: DT
pins.function: Dead-time set. A resistor to ground draws a current from an internal 2.25 V reference, and that current sets the gap between the two gate outputs. The gap never falls below 120 ns, so a shorted pin still leaves 120 ns.

pins.name: RT
pins.function: Frequency control. The current drawn out of this pin sets the switching frequency. A resistor to ground fixes the least current and so the minimum frequency; the feedback optocoupler collector goes to this pin, and a resistor in series with it caps the current and so the maximum frequency.

pins.name: OC
pins.function: Overcurrent sense. Above 1 V both gate outputs are pulled low; once it falls under 0.6 V switching resumes through soft start. Above 2 V the part latches off until VCC drops below the UVLO level.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start and on/off. A capacitor to ground sets the soft-start time. Holding the pin under 1 V turns the part off. Soft start runs after every fault clears: bias overvoltage, UVLO, overcurrent and overtemperature.

pins.name: GD2
pins.function: Gate drive output 2; with GD1 it drives the primary of a gate drive transformer for the half-bridge.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Bias supply, below 20 V, bypassed to ground with a 1 μF capacitor.

pins.name: GD1
pins.function: Gate drive output 1; with GD2 it drives the primary of a gate drive transformer for the half-bridge.

circuits.title: 300 W, 12 V LLC half-bridge converter (HPA341 design)
circuits.description: A 390 V dc input feeds a half-bridge of two MOSFETs, Q1 and Q2. U2 drives them through a gate drive transformer T3: each output pin GD1, GD2 has an NPN/PNP emitter-follower pair (Q4/Q5, Q6/Q7) and a 1 uF dc-blocking capacitor, and on the gate side each MOSFET has a 3.30 Ω gate resistor bypassed by a BAS16 for fast turn-off and a 10.0 kΩ gate-source resistor. The switch node drives the resonant tank: current transformer T1 (burden R1, probe jack TP2), resonant inductor L1 (55 uH), main transformer T2 (Lm 280 uH) and resonant capacitors C4 and C5 (24 nF in all) to primary ground. The ac voltage on the resonant capacitors is coupled by C11 and R7+R8, rectified by D3/D5 and filtered by R27 and C28 onto OC. The centre-tapped secondary is rectified by two rectifier cards DB1 and DB2, joined to the output through jumpers JP3-JP7, and filtered by C6, C7, L2 and C8 for 12 V at 25 A on J4. A TL431 (U3) with divider R13, R16, R24 and compensation R20/C19 drives optocoupler U1, whose collector pulls on FB; FB meets RT through R23 (511 Ω, maximum frequency) while R25 (2.37 kΩ) sets the minimum frequency and R21 (12.1 kΩ) the dead time. Comparator U5:A compares a divided output (R30, R29) with a 5.1 V zener and, on overvoltage, lights optocoupler U4, which pulls SS low; S1 also grounds SS. VCC comes from an external 12 V supply through D7 (clamped by D8, 15 V) or from the auxiliary winding of T2 through D4 and the Q3 regulator (12 V zener D9). C9 (4.7 nF) bridges primary and secondary grounds through JP8.

operation.text: Switching frequency is variable from 40 kHz to 350 kHz. The minimum frequency is programmable to within 4% over temperature, or 3% from -20 °C to 105 °C, and the maximum frequency is programmable too. The gate driver is built in, sourcing 0.4 A and sinking 0.8 A, enough to drive a gate drive transformer directly.

A controller for LLC resonant half-bridge converters, made for DC-DC stages of 100 W to 1 kW. It regulates by moving the switching frequency, has programmable dead time, soft start, minimum and maximum frequency, and protects against overcurrent (two levels), bias undervoltage and overvoltage, and overtemperature, all in an 8-pin SOIC.

Soft start runs at start-up and after every fault, raising the switching frequency so the tank current stays limited and switching stays at zero voltage. Pulling SS under 1 V turns the part off. When released, SS charges from its own current source; above 1.2 V gate pulses begin and soft start begins. Below 1.2 V the pin sources 175 µA to shorten the delay, above it 5 µA. During soft start the frequency depends on both the RT current and the SS voltage; once SS reaches 4 V, the RT current alone sets it. After a restart, GD2 is the first output to go high.

When OC rises above 1 V the power stage stops; when it falls under 0.6 V the gate drive restarts with soft start. Above 2 V the part latches off, and only taking VCC below the UVLO level clears the latch. Load current can be sensed indirectly from the ac voltage across the resonant capacitor, which follows the load current: a network of Cs and Rs couples it, D1 and D2 rectify it and Rp with Cp turn it into a filtered voltage on OC. Because the sizing rests on the first-harmonic model, the values need checking on real hardware.

The half bridge runs from a square wave of close to 50% duty at variable frequency, which a gate drive transformer carries to both MOSFETs. The transformer needs no separate gate-drive supply, keeps the layout simple, cannot shoot through because of its coupling and has no latch-up. The two outputs are trimmed to differ in on time by less than 50 ns, since asymmetry unbalances the rectifier currents; a dc-blocking capacitor in series with the transformer primary is still advised to keep it out of saturation during fast transients.
Junction temperature is watched all the time. Above 160 °C both gate outputs are held low; below 140 °C the gate drive restarts with soft start.

At light load the loop pushes the frequency up, but energy reaching the output through the transformer and rectifier-junction capacitances can lift the output above regulation, and more frequency does not help. So when the loop asks for more than 350 kHz the gate drive stops; when it asks for less than 330 kHz, switching resumes. Capping the maximum frequency below 350 kHz keeps burst mode from ever starting.

Above 10.5 V on VCC the part enables and, once no fault remains, starts with soft start. Below 9.5 V it enters UVLO with both gate outputs pulled low. Above 20 V it enters VCC overvoltage protection, outputs low, and recovers through soft start when VCC falls back under 18 V.

The LLC converter is a series resonant converter that uses the transformer's magnetizing inductance. It keeps zero-voltage switching over wide input and load, above and below resonance, which keeps it out of the zero-current region. Efficiency is best near the resonant frequency at nominal input; lowering the frequency raises the gain, so regulation holds as the input sags, which suits it to running from a boost PFC stage through line dropouts. Gain is analysed with the first harmonic approximation (FHA), treating all tank voltages and currents as sinusoids at the switching frequency.

Soft switching relies on the tank current at turn-off to discharge the MOSFET junction capacitances. More turn-off current discharges them faster but adds turn-off loss; less current needs more time. Choosing the dead time well keeps the turn-off current low while keeping zero-voltage switching. One resistor from DT to ground sets it; the minimum is 120 ns.

The frequency is proportional to the current out of RT. A resistor from RT to ground sets the least current (minimum frequency) and a resistor in series with the optocoupler sets the most current (maximum frequency).

VCC needs low-ESR ceramic decoupling placed directly from VCC to GND, in X7R or better; X5R may do in some temperature ranges, though it loses capacitance with heat and dc bias. The recommended part is 1 µF, 0805, 50 V, X7R, ideally with a 100 nF, 0603, 50 V, X7R in parallel. Higher voltage ratings are fine; 25 V parts are not recommended because of their capacitance loss under bias.

Use four layers. Place the 1 µF ceramic between VCC and GND as close as possible, with direct tracks to both pins. Keep CSS, RDT, Rp, Cp, RT1 and RT2 tight against the controller. Feed VCC from a regulated bias supply.
